whatWorks: Seed 5134 is the brief rendered correctly and should be the reference the rest is pulled toward: a six-fold ring of members held clear of a doubled inner ring, whose rotational order still reads at 120px without any individual member resolving.

The centred concentric construction is genuinely constant across all twelve seeds and all three market rows, so a token stays recognisably the same object between neutral, stress and recovery - the identity anchor is holding and must not be traded away for state legibility.

The single thin slate ring is the one fine-line element in the picture and it is the only thing currently reading as instrument-like rather than as a filled shape; its weight and its cool desaturated hue against the brass are correct.

findings.whatFails: The ground is not dark. Every tile is a bright ochre radial glow that is at its LIGHTEST in the centre of the frame, exactly where the mechanism sits, so brass members are drawn on a brass-coloured field one or two steps of value away from themselves. In dev-single-512 the central hexagon is nearly the same luminance as the ground behind it and only the slate ring and the black core survive.
findings.why: The brief and the paletteIntent both say brass and slate over a DARK ground, and negativeSpace says the margin outside the outer ring isolates the mechanism against nothing. A centre-bright vignette does the opposite: the brightest region of the picture is the empty space, so the margin competes with the assembly instead of isolating it, and the brass has no dark to be legible against.
findings.specificChange: Darken the ground to a near-black slate well below the darkest brass value, and remove the centre-bright radial vignette entirely (or invert it so the frame centre is the darkest point rather than the lightest). Reserve the top of the value range for the brass line work alone, so the only bright marks in the frame are drawn ones.
findings.keep: Keep the warm brass hue of the members and the cool desaturated slate of the outer ring exactly as they are - the two-material pairing is right, it is only the field behind it that is wrong.

findings.whatFails: Almost everything is a solid fill. The central polygons in 5265, 5789, 6313 and 6444 are flat filled hexagons, 6182 and 6051 are flat filled discs, and 5396 and 5920 are piles of filled blocks. The outer circle is the only stroked element in most seeds, so the picture is made of mass with one line drawn around it.
findings.why: paletteIntent requires the drawing to be carried in fine line so the whole reads as engineering rather than as mass, and the medium is a machined mechanism. A filled disc with a ring around it reads as a badge or a planet, not as an escapement; density also asks that individual radial members stay legible, which a solid silhouette cannot deliver.
findings.specificChange: Replace the solid fills on the radial members and on the central polygon with hairline strokes at the same weight family as the outer ring, and remove fill entirely from anything outside the centre. Keep filled area only for the small centre stop, so filled mass appears exactly once per token.
findings.keep: Keep the shape vocabulary and the outer-to-inner scale relationships as drawn - the hexagon, disc and rosette silhouettes are fine as outlines and should not be redesigned while they are being unfilled.

findings.whatFails: Most seeds carry a single slate circle around one centred blob, not nested rings of turned members. 5265, 5789, 6313, 6444, 6182 and 6051 show no repeated radial member at any angular interval at all, and where inner structure exists it is a dark tangled knot at the centre (5003, 5265, the 512 render) that is the highest-contrast, highest-detail element in the frame.
findings.why: The motifTranslation is nested concentric rings of radial members, each ring a turned repetition of the last, and focalHierarchy says the outer ring dominates with inner rings descending as secondary structure and the centre reading as a stop. A ring plus a knot inverts that: the centre is loudest, there is no descent, and the rotational logic that is supposed to be the whole subject is absent.
findings.specificChange: Increase the minimum ring count to three concentric rings per token and require every ring to carry radial members at the token's symmetry order, each ring turned from the one inside it by a steady angular step. Decrease stroke weight monotonically from the outer ring inward, and narrow the centre to a small quiet stop rather than the darkest cluster in the frame.
findings.keep: Keep 5134's proportions as the target: the outer ring standing clear of its members with a real gap, and the members reading as a rhythm rather than as a continuous edge.

findings.whatFails: On the 120px sheet, 5003, 5265, 5527, 5789, 6313 and 6444 all read as the same picture - a small gold polygon inside a thin grey circle on an identical gold glow. Half the collection is one work repeated. The ground, the overall footprint, the palette and the centre-to-ring ratio are effectively constant, so nothing but 5134, 5920, 6051 and 5396 has a distinct thumbnail.
findings.why: variationStrategy says tokens differ FIRST in rotational symmetry order, and thumbnailIntent says the concentric ring silhouette and its rotational order survive at 120px. Symmetry order is precisely the axis that is invisible here, so the declared primary variation contributes nothing at the size the collection is actually browsed at.
findings.specificChange: Spread the rotational symmetry order across a wide declared range (3 through 12 rather than the near-constant order visible now) and make the outer ring's member count the largest silhouette event in the frame. Widen the outer-ring diameter range so tokens also differ in overall footprint, and add ring-count variation as the second axis so a three-ring token is unmistakable from a one-ring token in a grid.
findings.keep: Keep the centred construction, the shared dark ground and the brass/slate pairing constant across seeds - those are the declared identity anchors and the diversity must come from order, ring count and member silhouette, never from recolouring tokens.

findings.whatFails: Stress does not loosen the mechanism, it inflates it. 5003 stress becomes a filled disc that swallows its own ring, 5265 stress grows a hexagon LARGER than the ring it was inside, and 5134 stress pushes its outer members off the top and bottom edges of the frame where they are cut by the viewBox. 5396 and 5920 collapse into an unreadable pile of overlapping blocks with no member separable from its neighbour.
findings.why: marketTransformation says the rings SEPARATE and the members spread apart under volatility, and composition requires the figure to be held clear of the frame edge with a margin that isolates it. Growth into the frame edge is the opposite of separation: it destroys the margin, inverts the outer-ring hierarchy, and at 120px reads as a zoom rather than as a mechanism coming apart.
findings.specificChange: Pin the outer ring diameter to a fixed fraction of the frame (no more than 0.8 of the shorter side) in every market state so no state can reach the edge, and express volatility by increasing the radial gap BETWEEN rings and the angular gap between adjacent members while holding that outer envelope constant. Decrease member size as the gaps widen so total ink stays flat and nothing collides.
findings.keep: Keep stress obviously different from neutral at 120px - the state change currently reads clearly at browse size and that legibility must survive the switch from growth to separation, along with recovery settling back toward the neutral spacing.

overall: The construction logic is sound and one seed (5134) shows the brief working exactly as written, but the material reading is inverted almost everywhere else: the brief asks for brass and slate line work on a dark ground and what is rendered is brass-coloured mass on a centre-bright brass glow, so the emptiest part of every frame is also its brightest and the mechanism has nothing to be legible against. Because the members are filled rather than stroked and most tokens carry a single ring around a centred blob, the rotational logic that is supposed to be the entire subject is absent from roughly two thirds of the seeds - which is also why half the 120px sheet reads as one repeated badge, since symmetry order is the declared primary variation axis and it is the one thing invisible at browse size. The market rows compound it: stress inflates the assembly into the frame edge and into collision instead of separating the rings, so the state change arrives as a zoom rather than as a mechanism loosening. Fixing the ground value and unfilling the members would recover most of the engineering read on its own; raising ring count and spreading symmetry order would then give the thumbnails somewhere to differ.
